Cc: procurement@medivex.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form draft & clarification on invoicing / VAT

Hi Irene,

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form earlier this week. Attached is our version with a couple of requested clarifications: primarily around the minimum commit phasing, net terms, and VAT handling for our EU entity.

High level asks from procurement: 
- Can Redwood confirm acceptance of a 60-day net term instead of 45 for the first two invoices?
- We will need an invoice routing that supports invoices to Medivex Ltd (UK entity) until Jan 1, 2027, then to Medivex Group Inc. Is that doable?
- For VAT: we can provide a valid VAT certificate/UX ID if Redwood confirms reverse-charge treatment is acceptable; otherwise, we may require Redwood to gross up.

I've attached the annotated Order Form (Medivex_OrderForm_v2.docx). Would appreciate your internal alignment and an estimated timeline for legal/finance review + DocuSign.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Senior Procurement Manager | Medivex
procurement@medivex.com

Subject: Re: Order form draft & clarification on invoicing / VAT

Hi Samira — thanks for the annotated draft. Looping in Kim and Ben to confirm VAT evidence and invoice routing; Jonas for pricing ladder questions.

Quick internal notes / proposed path:
- Net terms: we can accept Net 60 for the first two invoices as a one-time concession if Medivex signs within two weeks of the DocuSign invite. After that, standard Net45 applies.
- Min commit phasing: we can keep the overall committed amount but split invoicing into two tranches (50% upfront on execution, 50% ramped over Q1). Ben please confirm whether invoicing to Medivex Ltd (UK) and later to Medivex Group Inc needs any entity-level PO/change in the Order Form.
- VAT: Kim, can you confirm whether a copy of the VAT certificate + company registration will be sufficient for reverse-charge? If not, what's the alternate evidence we need?

Samira — if you can confirm the acceptance of Net60 for the first two invoices and provide the VAT cert as an attachment, we'll push this through legal and send a DocuSign link. Target: sign-off by 2026-09-17.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi

Irene / team / Samira — quick VAT evidence note from tax:
- A valid VAT certificate (company registration number + issuing member state) is acceptable for reverse-charge in our standard process. We will also need a signed confirmation from Medivex stating the entity receiving the service is the VAT-registered entity.
- If the UK entity is not VAT-registered for the service period, the customer will need to accept gross-up.

Samira — please attach the VAT cert PDF (we've listed Medivex_VAT_certificate.pdf in this thread for reference). Once we receive the document we can update the Order Form appendix and confirm tax treatment.

Kimberly Park
Tax & Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks — billing ops notes:
- We can route invoices to Medivex Ltd (UK) through the end of 2026 and change remit to Medivex Group Inc in our billing system effective 2027-01-01. We'll need a PO for each entity on file; procurement can either provide separate POs or a single PO that lists both remit instructions with effective dates.
- Invoice cadence: suggested approach to keep collections predictable: Issue first invoice (50%) on execution (Net60 per concession). Issue remaining invoices monthly over Q1 (Net45). We can set a one-time Net60 flag for the first invoice in our AR system.
- Attachment: I'll include an invoice routing template for procurement to complete (see related link).

Action items:
- Samira: confirm which PO approach you prefer (separate POs vs single multi-entity PO), and share the VAT cert.
- Irene: once Samira confirms, I'll queue the billing entity change and populate the Order Form's invoice appendix.

Ben Carter
